projectlens.title: ProjectLens
projectlens.summary: Browser-local change assurance with cited-precedent RAG: compare a change pack with its schedule, retrieve similar past decisions with sources, then record the human response.
projectlens.problem: Change packs and schedules drift apart before board meetings. ProjectLens loads both in the browser, surfaces the largest conflicts with source dates, retrieves comparable past decisions (Gemini + LangGraph, traced in LangSmith), and records the human decision only after a Use/Ignore gate.
points: One-click Northstar demo on GitHub Pages — XER stay in the browser; no upload.
Cited-precedent RAG (LangGraph retrieve → Gemini brief → LangSmith traces) with a human Use/Ignore gate before the decision register.
Pytest + Playwright in CI; public Pages hosts the deterministic demo; live Gemini retrieve runs via local `make precedent-rag`.
projectlens.note: Demo fixtures are synthetic. GitHub Pages is static — live hybrid retrieve needs the local FastAPI sidecar (or a configured API URL).

quicksupply.title: QuickSupply
quicksupply.summary: A supply-cover workflow for requests, agencies, teacher offers, compliance, and live status — now a public repo with a recorded agency demo.
quicksupply.problem: School cover coordination can become a spreadsheet-and-message chain. QuickSupply shapes the job around request intake, sequential agency assignment, teacher availability, compliance checks, and status updates.
points: Separates school, agency, and teacher workflows instead of flattening them into one admin view.
Uses live status updates so bookings can move without manual chasing.
Public source plus a muted agency walkthrough on this preview page.
quicksupply.note: Public product repo. The video is a walkthrough of the agency workflow on synthetic/demo data.

england.title: Can England Win It
england.summary: An interactive World Cup scenario simulator kept public as a bit of fun — with an honest postmortem after the event.
england.imageAlt: Can England Win It scenario simulator screenshot
england.problem: Tools built for a single event go stale after it. This app ran 10,000 seeded simulations per scenario, and was archived with a postmortem instead of being left to rot.
points: Seed-deterministic simulation with tests for bounds, monotonicity and uncertainty ranges.
Recorded walkthrough on this preview — npm test runs in CI.
POSTMORTEM.md explains why the project was closed honestly after the tournament.
england.note: Public fun project. Scenario tool, not a forecast or betting product.

lakehouse.title: Marketing ML Lakehouse
lakehouse.summary: A local analytics loop that moves raw marketing CSVs through DuckDB, model training, checks, and a dashboard.
lakehouse.problem: Many analytics demos stop at a notebook. This repo packages the full local loop: ingest raw marketing data, model it, check it, and expose it through a dashboard.
points: Two commands from clone to running pipeline, using CSV fixtures committed to the repo.
CI rebuilds the whole DuckDB lakehouse from the demo data and runs shape, tolerance and leakage checks.
The Pages demo states on the page that metrics come from committed fixtures, not a connected ad account.
lakehouse.note: Local demo pipeline and browser console — not a hosted SaaS product.

sentence.title: Sentence Similarity Analysis
sentence.summary: Embedding shortlists for FAQ match and precedent-style retrieval — the same caveat you need before trusting a ProjectLens RAG answer.
sentence.problem: Embedding similarity is useful for shortlisting, but it is not proof. This notebook shows ranking that helps retrieval and where it still misleads.
points: Transformer embeddings + cosine ranking over a fixed corpus.
Use it as the retrieval half of RAG / FAQ / similar-ticket flows.
Non-goal: top-1 similarity is not a verified fact — cite sources next.
sentence.note: Study notebook that supports the ProjectLens RAG direction: retrieve with caveats, then human/source check.

recommender.title: Swipe Recommender Lab
recommender.summary: Collaborative filtering on swipe-style implicit feedback with temporal holdouts and Top-K metrics — a recommender-systems signal, not a dating product.
recommender.problem: Random-split recommenders look good and fail in time. This lab uses temporal holdouts so ranking quality is honest.
points: Implicit feedback from swipe-style interactions.
Temporal holdout Top-K evaluation in CI.
Shows CF / ranking discipline useful beyond dating (marketplace, content, shortlists).
recommender.note: Offline ranking lab on synthetic/demo swipes. Not a live dating app.

pyspark.title: PySpark Kafka Streaming
pyspark.summary: Compact PySpark + Kafka patterns for ops event streams — cover status, booking updates, telemetry fan-in.
pyspark.problem: Streaming tutorials are often too large to read. These scripts show the shape for live status feeds without a platform dump.
points: DataFrame + Structured Streaming paths that CI can compile.
Maps to live booking/cover status buses and ops telemetry.
Kafka round-trip via Docker when you want producer/consumer.
pyspark.note: Technical example for event-shaped products (QuickSupply status, Happening ingest) — not a packaged platform.

hr.title: HR Performance Analytics
hr.summary: A Power BI dashboard package for headcount, sales performance, absence, and stakeholder-ready reporting.
hr.problem: Dashboard work is only useful when someone can inspect the handoff material. This package keeps screenshots, PBIX files, data, and commentary together.
points: Covers summary, sales, and absence views.
Includes PBIX files and a methodology PDF for inspection.
The sample CSV is synthetic and the README says the automated checks cover only its schema.
hr.note: Handoff package: open PBIX and PDFs in the repo. There is no live web demo.
